title: DM revisions exceed three times the quoted error sum in 206 of 428 selected CHIME bursts
abstract: We compare dispersion measures for the same events in CHIME/FRB Catalogs 1 and 2. In 206 of 428 selected matched bursts, the absolute revision exceeds three times the sum of the quoted errors. The fraction is 48.1 percent, with a source-cluster bootstrap interval of 43.4 to 52.7 percent. The sum bounds the standard deviation of a difference for any correlation if the quoted errors are valid marginal standard deviations. The result persists in single-component and unchanged-scattering samples. It shows processing sensitivity beyond the quoted errors. It does not establish plasma evolution, an error in either release, or a new source. Event identity uses exact TNS names. Raw spectra and independent telescope data were not tested. Code, aggregate results, a figure, source hashes and retrieval steps are included. External records remain outside the publication.

display.caption: DM revisions and sample controls. Error bars show 95 percent source-cluster bootstrap intervals.
